title: Spanish
motto: The vibrant language of Cervantes, spoken across 20+ countries and 500M+ people worldwide.
description: Master Spanish through the official MCER / Instituto Cervantes curriculum spanning 20 leveled units across A1 (Beginner), A2 (Elementary), B1 (Intermediate), B2 (Upper-Intermediate), and C1/C2 (Mastery).

proverbOfDay.proverb: Dime con quién andas, y te diré quién eres.
proverbOfDay.translation: Tell me who you walk with, and I will tell you who you are.
proverbOfDay.context: A cornerstone proverb across the Hispanic world, celebrating integrity, community solidarity, and how our chosen social circle shapes our character.

cultureTips.title: The Art of 'La Sobremesa'
cultureTips.description: In Spain and Latin America, meals do not end when the dessert is finished. 'La sobremesa' is the relaxed, cherished conversation with family and friends around the table lasting for hours, discussing ideas and strengthening bonds.

cultureTips.title: The Subtle Shift: 'Tú' vs 'Usted'
cultureTips.description: While contemporary Spain leans heavily into casual 'tú' (tutear), respect for elders, professors, doctors, and formal institutions still calls for 'usted'. In Colombia and Costa Rica, 'usted' is used even among family members as a mark of warmth and deep esteem.

cultureTips.title: The Two Cheek Kisses: 'Dos besos'
cultureTips.description: In Spain, women greeting friends (and men greeting women) give two light cheek kisses—always starting on the right cheek, then the left. Men greeting men typically exchange a warm handshake and a pat on the shoulder.

cultureTips.title: The Inverted Question and Exclamation Marks (¿ and ¡)
cultureTips.description: Spanish is the only language in the world that brackets sentences with inverted opening punctuation (¿...?, ¡...!). Established by the Real Academia Española in 1754, this ingenious rule alerts the reader to intonation and cadence before speaking the first word.

cultureTips.title: Linguistic Diversity: The Four Co-official Languages
cultureTips.description: Article 3 of Spain's 1978 Constitution recognizes castellano as the official language of the State, while catalán (in Catalonia, Valencia, and the Balearics), gallego (in Galicia), and euskera (in the Basque Country and Navarre) hold co-official status, forming a treasured plurilingual heritage.

cultureTips.title: The Spanish Schedule: Late Lunches and Evening Dinners
cultureTips.description: Spain operates on a unique circadian schedule due to its geographical longitude. Lunch (la comida) takes place between 14:00 and 15:30 as the main meal of the day, while dinner (la cena) is rarely served before 21:00 or 22:00.

slangs.meaning: It's super cool / Awesome (Essential colloquialism across Spain).
slangs.example: Este nuevo proyecto de literatura mola un montón.

slangs.meaning: To have one's head in the clouds / Daydreaming during class.
slangs.example: Baja a la tierra, Lucas, estás en las nubes y no escuchas al profesor.

slangs.meaning: How lovely / How pretty and cool (Very popular in central Spain).
slangs.example: ¡Qué chulo el cartel que diseñaste para la revista digital!

slangs.meaning: Alright / Okay / Understood (The most frequent conversational pivot in Spain).
slangs.example: ¿Nos vemos en la biblioteca a las cinco? — ¡Vale, allí estaré!

slangs.meaning: Good vibes / Kind, relaxed person (Universally loved in Latin America).
slangs.example: La profesora de ciencias tiene muy buena onda con el alumnado.

slangs.meaning: Pure life / Everything is marvelous (Costa Rica's world-famous life philosophy).
slangs.example: ¿Cómo marchan tus estudios? — ¡Pura vida, aprendiendo a diario!

customFlashcards.back: Hello / Hi — standard universal greeting in Spanish for any time of day.
Good morning — used from dawn until lunchtime / noon.
Good afternoon — used from post-lunch / midday until sunset.
customFlashcards.example: Buenas tardes a todos los presentes.

customFlashcards.back: Good evening / Good night — used both as a nighttime greeting and farewell.
Pleased to meet you — polite formula upon being introduced.
Delighted to meet you — agrees in gender with the speaker (male: -o, female: -a).
customFlashcards.example: Encantada de conocerte, me llamo Carmen.

customFlashcards.back: What is your name? (informal 2nd person singular).

customFlashcards.example: Me llamo Mateo y soy de Valencia.

customUnits.title: Unidad 1: Primeros Pasos (First Steps)
customUnits.subtitle: Presente de indicativo (ser, estar, verbos regulares), saludos, alfabeto, números y países.

lessons.title: Lección 1: Saludos, Alfabeto y Verbos Esenciales (Ser vs. Estar)
lessons.description: Aprende los saludos básicos, el alfabeto en español y la conjugación en presente de los verbos 'ser' y 'estar'.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es la forma correcta del verbo 'ser' para 'Yo'?
questions.explanation: 'Yo soy' es la primera persona del singular del verbo irregular 'ser'.

questions.prompt: Empareja los pronombres personales con la forma correcta de 'ser':
Hola, me ___ Mateo y soy de España.
questions.sentence: Hola, me ___ Mateo y soy de España.
questions.explanation: Para decir el nombre usamos 'me llamo' (del verbo reflexivo llamarse).

questions.prompt: Ordena las palabras para formar una presentación básica:
questions.explanation: Estructura canónica: Saludo + sujeto + verbo ser + atributo + complemento.

lessons.title: Lección 2: Presentaciones, Países, Nacionalidades y Números
lessons.description: Aprende a indicar tu procedencia, expresar nacionalidades con concordancia de género y dominar los números del 0 al 100.

questions.prompt: Ordena las palabras para indicar país de origen:
questions.explanation: Para expresar procedencia se usa 'ser + de + país': Mi profesor es de Colombia.

questions.prompt: Empareja cada país con la nacionalidad correspondiente (masculino):
Si María nació en México, ¿cuál es su nacionalidad en femenino?
questions.explanation: Las nacionalidades concuerdan en género con el sujeto: María es mexicana.

questions.prompt: Tengo ___ años y mi hermano tiene quince.
questions.sentence: Tengo ___ años y mi hermano tiene quince.
questions.explanation: El número cardinal para 20 es 'veinte'. La edad en español se expresa con el verbo 'tener'.
